paite: Tu in unaute aw, khalam thilpiak thute na theih louh uh ka ut kei hi.
heading: Khalam Thilpiakte
english: Now concerning spiritual things, brothers, I don’t want you to be ignorant.

paite: Zentelte na hih lai un bangchidan peuh a hon pi lai un leng, huai milim pau theiloute lam ah pimang in na om uh chih na thei uhi.
english: You know that when you were heathen, you were led away to those mute idols, however you might be led.

paite: Huaiziak in kuamah in, Pathian Kha a thu gen in, "Jesu hamsiat in om hen," achi ngei kei. Huan kuamah in, Kha Siangthou kia lou ngal in, "Jesu, Toupa ahi," achi ngei kei uh chih ka hon theisak hi.
english: Therefore I make known to you that no man speaking by God’s Spirit says, “Jesus is accursed.” No one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” but by the Holy Spirit.

paite: Huan thilpiak tuamtuam a-om a, Kha bel kikhat ahi.
english: Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.

paite: Nasepna tuamtuam leng a-om, himahleh Toupa khat ahi.
english: There are various kinds of service, and the same Lord.

paite: Nasepsakna tuamtuam leng a-om, himahleh Pathian khat ahi, mi tengteng a bangkim sempa ahi.
english: There are various kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.

paite: Himahleh Kha theihsakna michih kiphattuampih chiatna ding in piak ahi.
english: But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.

paite: Mi khat kiang ah Kha in pilna thu apia hi; midang kiang ah, huai Kha mah in theihna thu apia hi.
english: For to one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,

paite: Huan midang kiang a, huai Kha mah in, ginna apia a; midang kiang ah hihdamtheihna apia;
english: to another faith by the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healings by the same Spirit,

paite: midang kiang ah thillamdang hihtheihna, midang kiang ah thugenkholh theihna, midang kiang ah khate theihkak theihna, midang kiang ah pau tuamtuamte, midang kiang ah pautuamte hilhchetna.
english: and to another workings of miracles, and to another prophecy, and to another discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of languages, and to another the interpretation of languages.

paite: Himahleh hiaite tengteng Kha khat leh akikhat mah in, michih kiang ah adeih bang zel a hawm in asem hi.
english: But the one and the same Spirit produces all of these, distributing to each one separately as he desires.

paite: Pumpi i chih khat ahi a, hiang anei a, pumpi hiangte tengteng, tam mah le uh, pumpi khat ahi a; Khrist leng huchibang mah ahi.
heading: Pumpi A Kipan Sin Ding
english: For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.

paite: I vek un pumpi khat a om ding in Kha khat a baptis in i omta ua, Judate hiam, Grikte hiam, sikhate hiam sikha lou hiam; huan i vek un Kha khat a kipan dawnsak in i omta uhi.
english: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free; and were all given to drink into one Spirit.

paite: Pumpi i chih hiang khat kia hilou in tampi ahi zaw hi.
english: For the body is not one member, but many.

paite: Khepek in, "Khut ka hih louh ziak in pumpi a pang ka hi kei," chileh, huai thu ziak in pumpi a pang lou ahi tuan kei hi.
english: If the foot would say, “Because I’m not the hand, I’m not part of the body,” it is not therefore not part of the body.

paite: Huan bil in, "Mit ka hih louh ziak in pumpi a pang ka hi kei," chileh, huai thu ziak in pumpi a pang lou ahi tuan kei hi.
english: If the ear would say, “Because I’m not the eye, I’m not part of the body,” it’s not therefore not part of the body.

paite: Pumpi tengteng mit hi vek taleh gingzakna koi ah a-om dia? Avek in gingzakna hitaleh, gimzakna koi ah a-om dia?
english: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be?

paite: Himahleh Pathian in hiang khempeuh pumpi ah a-utna peuh ah a-omsak chiatta hi.
english: But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body, just as he desired.

paite: Huchi in huai tengteng hiang khat kia hileh pumpi pen koi ah a-om dia?
english: If they were all one member, where would the body be?

paite: Himahleh hiang tampi ahi zaw uh, himahleh pumpi khat kia ahi.
english: But now they are many members, but one body.

paite: Huan mit in, khut kiang ah, "Bangmah in ka hon deih kei," achi thei kei; lu in leng khepekte kiang ah, "Bangmah in ka hon deih kei," achi thei sam kei hi.
english: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”

paite: Huchih nak sang in, pumpi hiang hat dia kilawm lou pente akiphamohzaw mahmah uhi.
english: No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.

paite: Huchi in pumpi hiang pahtawi tham louh zaw a i sehte, huaite ngei i pahtawi zaw uhi; huan i hiang kilawmloute'n kilawmna thupizaw amu zel uhi.
english: Those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, on those we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant modesty,

paite: I hiang kilawmte'n bel huchibang a hih akiphamoh kei uhi. Pathian in, kilawmna nei lou hiang pahtawi zawk ding in, pumpi alemkhawm hi.
english: while our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part,

paite: Huchi a pumpi a kikhenna om lou a, ahiangte'n kibangtak a akibuaipihtuah theih zawkna ding un.
english: that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.

paite: Huchi in hiang khat in athuakleh hiang tengteng in athuakpih a, hiang khat pahtawi a a-omleh hiang dangte'n akipahpih zel uhi.
english: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.

paite: Huchi in noute Khrist pumpi na hi ua, ahiangte na hi chiat lai uhi.
english: Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.

paite: Huan Pathian in khenkhat saptuam lak ah ahon koih a, akhatna ah sawltakte, anihna ah thugenkholte, athumna ah sinsaktute akoih a; huai nung in thillamdang hihte a-om a; huai nung in hihdamtheihna thilpiakte, panpih theihna thilpiakte, vaihawm siamna thilpiakte, pau tuamtuam a thugentheihna thilpiakte a-om nawn hi.
english: God has set some in the assembly: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, and various kinds of languages.

paite: Avek un sawltak ahi uhia? Avek un thugenkholmi ahi uhia? Avek un sinsaktu ahi uhia?
english: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?

paite: Avek un thillamdang hihmi ahi uhia? Avek un hihdamtheihna thilpiakte ahi uhia? Avek un pautuamte in thu agen uhia? Avek un thu hilhchianmi ahi uhia?
english: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with various languages? Do all interpret?

paite: Thilpiak thupipente lunggulh mahmah zaw un. Huan lampi hoihsem ka hon ensak ding hi.
english: But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.
